other_world_rule: the world that differs from the fossil's native image (64-bit <-> 32-bit)
positive_control: md5-rfc1321 must report DIVERGES; if it does not, the method is broken
note: A world probe never persists; recorded classifications are untouched. INCONCLUSIVE_BUILD is not evidence of environment-dependent correctness.

rows.mechanism: RFC 1321 global.h: typedef unsigned long int UINT4 -- identified, single line.

rows.caveat: tinycc DIVERGES under a valid control: it builds in both worlds, passes its oracle at 64-bit and fails it at 32-bit. But the MECHANISM is NOT established. tinycc is a C compiler, so running it in a 32-bit userland changes its code-generation target, not merely its own integer widths. This is a real measured environment dependence; it is NOT demonstrated to be the same single-line width assumption that breaks md5-rfc1321, where the responsible line is identified. Calling them the same defect class would be an inference, not a measurement.

coverage.not_tested_reason: The full 6-candidate run was KILLED by host memory pressure mid-way. Rather than report the earlier run (whose positive control had FAILED, because it compared md5's native 32-bit world against itself), this minimal re-run covers the control plus the single candidate that run had flagged. cjson-1.7.18, femtolisp, espresso-logic and zchaff-2007 remain UNTESTED, along with the heavier set already named.
